title: Embedded Software Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build from C/C++ and computer architecture into microcontrollers, firmware, RTOS, embedded Linux, device drivers and production-grade embedded software.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a four-year B.Tech/B.E. from 2026–2030. If an honours/research pathway is available, use the additional depth for embedded Linux, RTOS, operating systems, computer architecture, automotive software, IoT or edge computing.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build strong C/C++, computer architecture, microcontroller, firmware, debugging and operating-system fundamentals.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Move into firmware, RTOS, embedded Linux, device drivers, automotive software, IoT or systems software.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior embedded software, platform, systems or firmware architecture roles.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine embedded software with edge AI, cybersecurity, heterogeneous computing, advanced SoCs and connected systems.

rows.text: C programming, data structures, digital logic and computer fundamentals
Embedded C, interrupts, timers, ADC/DAC, PWM and memory
UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, debugging and version control
RTOS, scheduling, concurrency, synchronization and memory management
Embedded Linux, device drivers, shell and networking
Major embedded software project + interview preparation

blocks.text: 4-year honours variant
Use the additional academic depth for embedded Linux, operating systems, RTOS, computer architecture, automotive systems, FPGA/SoC development, edge AI, cybersecurity or embedded systems research.

rows.text: C/C++, MCU/SoC, model optimisation, edge inference

blocks.text: Continue developing expertise in heterogeneous SoCs, edge AI, embedded cybersecurity, real-time systems, automotive software, robotics, industrial systems and hardware-software co-design.
